history.period: Built 1660-1675 CE by Maharaja Govinda Manikya (r. 1660-1676)
history.summary: CSV town 'Udaipur' is CORRECT. This is the Tripura royal family's Bhuvaneswari temple on the eastern fringe of Udaipur town by the bank of the river Gomati (one crosses the Gomati to reach it), ~1.5 km from Udaipur, ~55 km from Agartala. Built by Maharaja Govinda Manikya in 1660-1675; the ruins of his palace lie nearby. Now under the control and supervision of the Archaeological Survey of India. The temple is immortalized in two of Rabindranath Tagore's plays - Rajarshi and Bisarjan (Visarjan) - with Maharaja Govinda Manikya himself featuring as a character. Architecture: a rare specimen of old temple architecture on a 3-ft-high lined terrace, with a four-chaala roof bearing stupa-like crowns on the doorway and inner chambers, the central stupa adorned with floral motifs. Dedicated to Goddess Bhuvaneswari, fourth of the ten Mahavidyas. COORDINATE FLAG: Tripura Tourism's own Google-maps pin for this temple (23.853930, 91.506407) points ~35 km north of Udaipur and is obviously erroneous; the coordinates used here are from a Matarbari/Udaipur map listing and should be verified on site.

name: Bhuvaneswari Temple
town: Udaipur (on the eastern fringe of Udaipur town, by the bank of the Gomati river)
town_description: Udaipur, in Gomati district on the Gomati river about 55 km from Agartala, was the capital of the Tripura kingdom under the Manikya dynasty before the capital shifted to Agartala. It is a cluster of 16th-17th century Manikya temples: the Shakti Peetha of Tripura Sundari at Matabari, the Bhuvaneswari temple by the Gomati, the Gunabati group of brick temples, and the old stone Jagannath temple by Jagannath Dighi.
